title: In 12 mice (OpenScope Neuropixels), illusory-contour images gave no response above matched non-aligned inducers in six visual areas, so the anatomical hierarchy could not order an IC signal
abstract: Question: in the Allen OpenScope Illusion data (DANDI:000248, 12 mice, Neuropixels), do the strength and timing of the illusory-contour (IC) signal follow the Harris et al. (2019) anatomical hierarchy across visual areas, as a feedback account predicts? Method: we decoded the inducer notches of each image from its pixels. Summed over two orientations, IC images and line-control (LC) images put the same notches on every inducer disc, so IC - LC is zero for any neuron that adds local features, also with large receptive fields. A plan was frozen and hashed before any IC response was computed (one amendment before any area result). Units with receptive fields at the stimulus centre (346 of 4,729 quality units) were tested with a mouse-level hierarchical bootstrap. Results: the configural signal was absent: mean d'(IC - LC) = -0.024 (95% CI -0.055 to 0.003), with no positive area mean; the real-edge control was positive (d' 0.070, CI 0.024 to 0.120; V1 0.11; onset 59-76 ms). The IC strength slope on hierarchy was 0.018 (CI -0.067 to 0.102); IC timing could not be measured. All pre-listed checks (all units, windows, Cre line, running, segment-insensitive units) and a post hoc gaze restriction gave IC - LC between -0.042 and +0.003. Post hoc, a Shin-style IC-encoder rule passed 49 of 330 centre-RF units, and the same rule with LC images labelled as IC also passed 49; its IC/real-edge orientation match is confounded by shared bottom-disc notches. A small negative IC - LC transient at 90-150 ms (post hoc window) is a hypothesis for new data. Limitations: one of four IC blocks; coarse 16 deg receptive-field map; few higher-area and no usable LP/LGd centre units; relative gaze rule; the two-photon results of Shin et al. were not tested.
